subject.title: Slack: Include file attachment metadata in inbound message delivery to agents

question: Should OpenClaw add a shared cross-channel inbound attachment metadata contract for agent context, or keep Slack file handling limited to placeholders, media paths, and `download-file`?
rationale: The useful fix changes an agent-facing channel/plugin contract, and repo policy treats plugin SDK and shared channel seams as product-sensitive boundaries rather than Slack-only implementation details.

options.title: Add Shared Attachment Metadata
options.body: Introduce a narrow `InboundAttachments`-style context shape and populate Slack id/name/MIME/size while preserving legacy media fields.

options.title: Add Slack-Only Metadata
options.body: Expose Slack file ids or file fields faster, accepting cross-channel drift and likely later migration work.

options.title: Keep Current Behavior
options.body: Continue relying on placeholders, `MediaPath` fields, docs, and `download-file` without adding a new agent metadata contract.

recommendation.title: Add Shared Attachment Metadata
recommendation.body: Introduce a narrow `InboundAttachments`-style context shape and populate Slack id/name/MIME/size while preserving legacy media fields.

likelyOwner.reason: The history pass points to steipete as the strongest current owner for the shared Slack/channel context boundary.
